reallocation.what: Same total budget. Grow the channels the model rates best, cut the ones it rates worst.

youtube_ask.what: New money: grow YouTube, the channel with the lowest cost per extra deal, by the largest step the optimizer allows. Every other channel stays as it is.

risks.text: The ranges are wide. The plan's range runs from a small gain to a large one, and the always-on channels' costs per deal span a wide band.

Non-brand search, LinkedIn, display and affiliates run every week in every market and never pause, so the data never show what happens without them. Their numbers lean on the model's starting assumptions. Every cut in the plan lands on these channels.

Meta pushes into the busy seasons in every market, the same weeks fleets shop anyway, so the model cannot tell Meta's effect from the season. Meta's range runs from almost nothing to a lot, and the plan grows Meta.

Paid media is likely under-credited. On simulated worlds with a known answer, this kind of model gave always-on channels too little credit until a test anchored them. If so, the cuts cost more than shown, and the plan's gain is smaller.
The model predicts weekly deals well on weeks it never saw, but a model can predict the total well and still split it wrongly between channels.
The YouTube ask rests on YouTube's on and off flights, the best measured channel. Each step up buys fewer deals than the last, and the model has not seen YouTube much past the size of the ask.

test.what: A spring market test of both questions behind the budget. In one group of markets, YouTube runs well above plan, a level the model has never seen. In a crossing group, non-brand search goes back to its 2023 pace. Each group is measured against the markets outside it, so every market counts for both. Markets were matched by size and picked by how well they tracked each other in past placebo tests.
test.decision_rule: Rules written down before the test: YouTube works if its lift is clearly positive. If pulling search back costs clearly more deals than the model expects, the rollout does not cut search below today's spend. Either way, both results go into the model as lift tests, the model is refit, and the rollout follows the refit model.
test.limits: The YouTube group is sized to see the lift the model expects. The search group is a guardrail: it only sees the drop if search is worth much more than the model thinks. YouTube runs past any level in the data, so the forecast there is a stretch.
test.readout: Late May, after the last deals in the window have had time to close.
test.dates: Test: February 2 to April 26. Deals counted through May 24. Readout from the data as of May 31.

recommendation: Now: approve the spring market test. It needs no new money: pulling search back saves more than the YouTube push costs.
In late May: the test result goes into the model, and the refit model sets the rollout for the rest of the year. Approve that rollout then, not now.
Not now: any big move in search. Search is the largest and least measured channel, and the test is how we measure it.
